PullRequest.Title: agentHost: don't allow moving a chat that hasn't sent a message
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #343966

A new nested session that was never sent (the New Nested Session composer) could be moved by drag and drop, Move Up/Down, Promote and the `move_session` tool, which swapped its composer. Per the decision on #343966, a chat that hasn't sent its first message can't be moved by any path, and becomes movable once its first turn starts (a chat mid-first-turn is movable).

**Host (authoritative)**
- `IChatMoveEligibility.notStarted`: a chat with loaded state and no turns and no active turn isn't advertised `movable`; recomputed on `ChatTurnStarted`.
- `_checkChatStarted` refuses move, reorder, move session and the `move_session` pre-check with the existing `NotStarted` refusal; Promote keeps its own check. Reworded host/tool/client messages beyond "promotion".
- A chat whose state isn't loaded (restored) counts as started, so cold moves still read no history.

**Client**
- `sessionsManagementService.canMoveChat` also refuses an untitled chat, so hosts without this fix (remote/older) don't offer drag, Move Up/Down or Promote for it.

**Intended behavior change in existing tests** (moving a never-run chat now needs a turn first; this is the #343966 decision):
- `agentService.test.ts`: chat/session creations in the move tests now use started helpers (`createStartedChat`/`createStartedSession`); `MovingAgent` restores one message; expectations adjusted in "a chat promotes only once its first turn started", the "deleting a chat that never moved" peer helper, "work deferred until a chat's turn ends", "checks a move as the host would refuse it", and the D4 confirmation test.
- `agentHostChatMovability.test.ts`: `addStartedChat` helper for existing tests.
- `agentHostChatMoveErrors.test.ts`, `sessionsListContextMenu.test.ts`: new message text.

**New tests:** every move path refuses an unsent chat and allows it after the first turn (agentService); movable once the first turn started, including while running (movability); untitled chat not movable on the client (sessionsManagementService). Each fails without its fix (mutation-checked).

**Validation** (whole folders): `platform/agentHost/test/node` 13466 passing; `sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser` 1005; `sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser` 1065; `sessions/services/sessions/test/browser` 657; eslint and `typecheck-client` clean. Live (isolated Code - OSS Agents window): an unsent New Nested Session row has no Promote to Session, Move Up/Down or other move entries, and dragging it onto another row moves nothing; after sending one message the row offers Promote to Session. Not covered live: the move_session refusal and nesting an unsent-only session (the agent cannot see the unsent draft; covered by unit tests). Base-build repro of the composer swap was not done.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed synchronous call path, per-event frequency, and linear session scan are directly established by the listener, dispatch implementation, update/_sourceContext code, and existing 100/400-chat perf tests. Exact milliseconds vary by catalog/worktree shape, but the repeated mechanism and scaling are not speculative.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work and temporary Maps/Sets/arrays allocated while rebuilding a session's movability context
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each ChatTurnStarted now performs O(C) work in the number of chats in the session: update() linearly finds the summary, _sourceContext() walks all chats and builds children/summary indexes, and sessions with per-chat worktrees scan the summaries again. This repeats for every turn, including all turns after the first; the repository's own perf tests model 100- and 400-chat sessions.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased prompt-start latency and CPU/GC pressure for sessions that have accumulated many nested chats
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this diff, ChatTurnStarted did not trigger AgentHostChatMovability.update(), so sending a message performed no session-wide movability rebuild on this path.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added action branch synchronously calls update(envelope.channel) for every ChatTurnStarted, although notStarted can only transition to false when a chat starts with no completed turns.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added RIGHT line 215 includes ActionType.ChatTurnStarted in the new event branch, and RIGHT line 217 invokes this.update(envelope.channel), placing the full recomputation on every turn start; neither operation existed on this event before the PR.
Findings.Title: Skip movability rebuilds after the first turn
Findings.Impact: Every subsequent message in a large multi-chat session synchronously rescans and reindexes the full chat catalog before dispatchServerAction returns and turn processing continues, delaying prompt submission; with hundreds of chats this repeated O(C) allocation/work occurs on every message even though movable is unchanged.
Findings.Evidence: AgentHostStateManager._applyAndEmit synchronously fires onDidEmitEnvelope; this new branch handles every ChatTurnStarted and calls update(). With no MovabilityPass, update() reaches _listedSummary(...).find over the session catalog, then _sourceContext(), which loops over state.chats and allocates children plus a Map of all summaries; _worktreeUsers() can loop all summaries again. setChatMovable() suppresses the notification when unchanged but only after this work. The added tests establish that the subsystem explicitly supports/scales against 100 and 400 chats.
Findings.Recommendation: Gate ChatTurnStarted recomputation to the actual notStarted transition (for example, after reduction only when the chat has zero completed turns and this is its first active turn), and similarly recompute truncation/load cases only when the notStarted boolean can change. This preserves immediate first-turn eligibility without rebuilding on every later message.

Scenarios.Scenario: Starting a turn in a peer or nested chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ChatTurnStarted is reduced and onDidEmitEnvelope fires synchronously; the new movability update completes before dispatch returns and before the turn reaches the agent/provider. The session-wide scan is therefore on the prompt-start critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the accepted turn to the agent host/provider through host.sendTurnMessage
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider dispatch per accepted turn
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Turn dispatch reached the provider without a movability catalog rebuild on ChatTurnStarted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The new synchronous O(C) movability rebuild delays reaching this pre-existing provider dispatch.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number C of chats/subagents retained in the source session; existing performance tests exercise 100 and 400 chats. The added cost is O(C) per turn, including every turn after the first.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each turn dispatch executes its recomputation synchronously. Concurrent turns on separate chats do not share a MovabilityPass or coalesce this work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: setChatMovable suppresses unchanged notifications, but _listedSummary, _sourceContext, and optional worktree indexes are rebuilt before that check; there is no warm-cache benefit between turns.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: synchronous event ordering and full-catalog scans are directly visible in the call path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact latency depends on catalog size, URI/worktree shape, and hardware; realistic 100/400-chat cardinalities are established by repository performance tests.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated-work regression: every message now pays session-wide CPU/allocation even though notStarted changes only on the first turn.

Scenarios.Scenario: Moving, reordering, promoting, or nesting a chat/session, including move_session pre-checks
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The move awaits source restoration when cold, validates ownership, then the new _checkChatStarted guard runs before anchor/destination checks. For a materialized chat this guard reads in-memory state and resolveChatState returns the same state immediately.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore cold source or destination session metadata/catalog needed for a move
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most the source and, for cross-session moves, destination per request; warm resident sessions perform no restore.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Moves already restored cold source/destination state before validation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing awaited move validation boundary; the diff does not add or multiply it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One source chat/session and at most one destination per requested move; moved subtree and worktree validation scale as before.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single move follows the existing ordered async validation path; cold per-entry state resolution is coalesced by AgentHostStateManager.inFlight.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Loaded sessions use resident state. Cold source/destination restoration uses existing data-only restoration behavior; the new started check does not force an unresolved restored chat to hydrate because it only calls resolve when getChatState already returned a state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: _checkChatStarted's conditional and resolveChatState's resident-state fast path are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Backend-specific restore latency varies, but the diff adds only an in-memory guard on the common loaded path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional reportable boundary regression; the correctness guard does not introduce cold history I/O on this path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resolving or paging restored chat history and truncating chat history
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The pre-existing resolver/history operation completes, then the new onDidResolveChatState or ChatTurnsLoaded/ChatTruncated listener synchronously recomputes movability before the action/promise finishes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the registered restored-chat resolver to load provider backing/history
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per successfully resolved chat due to cached entry.state; concurrent same-chat calls coalesce, while different chats resolve separately.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: History resolved without firing a movability recomputation afterward.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The boundary is pre-existing; the diff appends synchronous catalog recomputation after it and before resolution completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: O(C) catalog work for each resolved chat or history action, where C is chats in that session; multiple independently resolved chats do not share the generated indexes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Concurrent calls for the same chat share entry.inFlight; different chats can resolve independently and each performs its own synchronous recomputation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A chat's resolved state is cached after success and failures remain retryable. The new movability context itself is not cached across resolutions/pages.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the added O(C) post-resolution work; lower on how often many chats resolve together.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Bulk multi-chat hydration prevalence is not established, so this one-time-per-chat path is less clearly user-visible than the every-turn path.
Scenarios.Verdict: The work shares the reported repeated-work mechanism, but no separate finding is warranted because successful resolution is cached and bulk cardinality is uncertain.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rendering session-list move affordances and synchronizing a remotely started new chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: List/context-menu/drag checks synchronously read the chat status and provider movable flag; catalog status updates run one observable transaction.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: O(1) per rendered or interacted chat row; list rendering scales linearly as before.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Observable updates are transaction-coalesced; no asynchronous fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: AdditionalChat retains status and isNew observables; repeated non-Completed updates set the same false value and observable equality suppresses downstream changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the direct canMoveChat and AdditionalChat.update implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; these are in-memory observable reads/writes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression; the added status read/write is constant-time and does not introduce I/O or rendering fan-out.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 15 changed files and all diff pages. One medium-confidence-severity, high-mechanism-confidence repeated-work issue was submitted for synchronous O(C) movability rebuilding on every turn start; move validation, restored-state caching, and client affordance paths introduced no separate qualifying regression.
